entities.summary: Engelbert II of Nassau was a prominent count of Nassau and Vianden, serving as leader of the Privy council of the Duchy of Burgundy and a significant patron of the arts. Born in 1454, Engelbert II was a skilled soldier and politician who played a key role in the Duchy's governance. He was a major patron of the arts, supporting notable artists such as Hans Memling and Jan van Eyck. Engelbert II's reign was marked by significant cultural and artistic achievements, cementing his legacy as a notable figure in Western European history. Despite his passing in 1504, his artistic patronage continues to inspire art historians and enthusiasts alike. The intricate stone carvings he commissioned for the Burgundian court remain a testament to his enduring impact on the region's artistic heritage. Engelbert II's legacy is a poignant reminder of the transformative power of art and politics in shaping the course of human history.
